questions.question: In whose reign, the office of the Vakil was abolished?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaha Jahan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vakil** was the **royal deputy**. It was a post filled only twice under the **seven great Mughal emperors.**
 
• At the end of Akbar’s reign, the office of Vakil became ‘more or less honorific’ and continued till the reign of **Shah Jahan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Akbar**

 
 
• He reformed and strengthened his central administration and also centralized his financial system and homeithe tax-collection procedures.
 
• Though he never renounced Islam, he took an active interest in other religions, motivating Hindus, Zoroastrians and Christians as well as Muslims, to engage in religious discussions before him.
 
• Illiterate himself, he encouraged scholars, poets, painters and musicians, making his court the center of culture. 
 
 
 
• **Jahangir**
 
 
• **Jahangir** was a ruler interested in** literature, music, painting and architecture.**
 
• During his reign, British officers **William Hawkins and Sir Tomas Rowe** appeared in the Mughal court.
 
• Jahangir wrote his autobiography titled** 'Tujuk-e-Jahangiri'. **
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**​
 
 
• **Aurangzeb** was a ruler of **Mughal dynasty**.
 
• He was the son of Shah Jahan.
 
• He died in the year 1707.
 
• He imposed Jizya, a military tax on non-Muslims who were not fighting for Mughal Empire.
 
• He was succeeded by his son Bahadur Shah I.
 
• Aurangzeb was also known as** 'Zinda Pir' **because of his simple lifestyle.

questions.question: In sexual reproduction the male gametes are generally ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Both motile and small__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**In sexual reproduction, the male gametes (sperm cells) are generally both motile and small.**

 
• **Motility:** Male gametes are typically motile, meaning they have the ability to move on their own. This is primarily achieved through the flagellum, a whip-like structure that propels the sperm forward. The motility of sperm is crucial for successful fertilization, as sperm need to travel through the female reproductive tract to reach and penetrate the egg.
 
• **Size: **Male gametes are also generally smaller compared to female gametes (eggs). This small size allows sperm to be produced in large quantities and is advantageous for their role in fertilization. Smaller size facilitates easier movement and efficiency in reaching the egg, increasing the chances of successful fertilization.
 
• The human males have **23 pairs of chromosomes** including XY sex chromosomes. Therefore the male gametes has 22 chromosomes and either an X or a Y chromosome. Thus male gametes can be of two types:22+X or 22+Y.
 
• Female gametes are called** egg or ova.**
